newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Dostum forces join Masood's north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Dostum forces join Masood's north of Kabul.

text.p: Northern Uzbek General Abdul Rashid Dostum sent troops, tanks and artillery into Jabal os-Siraj on Thursday to honour a pledge to join forces of the ousted Afghan government north of Kabul, witnesses said.
As the troops meared the town from the north, a warplane bombed the area with one impact a few hundred metres (yards) behind a position north of the town occupied by reporters.
The arrival of Dostum's reinforcements was a fresh obstacle to attempts by the purist Islamic Taleban militia to press northward after seizing Kabul three weeks ago.
Any hope Taleban had of imposing their Pashtun-dominated control over former Afghan military chief Ahmad Shah Masood's Tajik and Dostum's Uzbek strongholds would seem to have ended.
"It means that if they (Taleban) insist on fighting they will face not only our troops but others as well," Abdullah (one name), a spokesman for Masood told reporters on Thursday in Jabal.

Masood staged an orderly retreat to his lair in the Pansjher Valley after being routed from Kabul by a surprise Taleban advance. Since then he has re-emerged and begun pushing back south towards Kabul.

But the advance has been bogged down and even suffered some setbacks in recent days as Masood seemed to pause around Bagram and Qarabagh about 60 km (40 miles) north of Kabul to wait for Dostum's forces to arrive.
"In the past four or five days there hasn't been much serious activity from our side," Abdullah explained.

"Taleban have moved a bit forward along the old road around Qarabagh and we have let them come. There were some civilian casualties from their rocketing and bombing. But Taleban has a small force there and I don't think it would be a problem for us to attack them."
Abdullah indicated that Dostum troops would take up positions south of Charikar towards the hotly contested Bagram junction and that artillery would be positioned behind the front in support.
The Dostum forces began arriving just before midday through the Salang pass when the first truck-mounted multiple-barrelled rocket-launcher took up a position just north of Jabal os-Siraj.
Most of Dostum's men have changed from their usual Russian uniforms into typical mujahideen clothing so as to better blend in with Masood's forces. Many were wearing green turbans.
This was said by Masood's men to be an effort not to offend local sensibilities which are strongly pro-Masood and traditionally have been anti-Dostum.
The air attack occurred just a short time later, the third in as many days against this strategic town situated 90 km (60 miles) north of Kabul.

The bombing did nothing to deter Dostum's forces and tanks accompanied by troop-carrying trucks clanked south through the town along the main highway. Reporters counted a dozen tanks passing in 30 minutes with more reportedly on their way down the Salang Pass.

Abdullah acknowledged that the Taleban have also been reinforcing their positions around Kabul in anticipation of a concerted attack by forces of the ousted government but said that was as much a sign of weakness as strength.
"After their big losses against us up here last week many of their commanders quit Kabul and took their men back to the areas from which they had come," the spokesman said.
"I am not sure about the numbers but of course there have been reinforcements. They needed them."
